newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end barely mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended a quiet afternoon on Friday barely mixed after failing to bulge out the day's ranges in either direction.

Afternoon erosion in U.S. Treasury bond futures from morning strength had a muted effect on stock index futures, which instead balanced losses in blue-chip issues against strength in over-the-counter and high-technology stocks.

"We are still seeing a divergence between blue-chip and OTC/small caps," said a floor broker on Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures. "Again, we are seeing what I would call a sort of rotational market."
"But on the flip side, I think the market has held in pretty well, given how far down the bonds have come," he added.
Morning weakness, which some tied to quarter-end portfolio adjustments and asset reallocation, gave way to a short-lived advance back up in early afternoon.
December S&P 500s reapproached the day's peak near the close in T-bond futures market, then stalled.
During the morning, traders saw aggressive dealer selling outright as well as some arbitrage sell programs when the premium over cash narrowed.
Fair value on Friday stood at about 5.60-point premium. Arbitrage buy programs would have needed about a 6.90-point premium. Sell programs required about 4.50 points over cash.
"It was getting blasted," said one floor broker of the morning's breakdown. "It traded very ugly, (with) no premium."
Stock futures reacted little when market sources reported that the final September University of Michigan consumer sentiment index slipped to 94.7 from a final 95.3 in August.

December S&P 500s ended off 0.55 pt at 691.40, Value Lines rose 3.25 pts to 643.95, Nikkei lost 65.0 to 21,510.0, Midcap rose 1.25 to 244.75, and NYSE Composite added 0.30 to 368.85. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
